chosen.title: Static Balance vs. Continuous Solvency
chosen.idea: A precise split-column technical spec sheet. The left side represents a legacy autonomous wallet: a static ledger state showing raw balance, zero risk computation, and dead capital ceiling. The right side displays an active agentic credit position on Vanna: continuous WAD-precision telemetry calculating Collateral USD over Debt USD, real-time derived Health Factor (1.428e18), and automated liquidation buffer thresholds. Stark, editorial, terminal-inspired styling with high-density data and minimal monochrome accents.
chosen.why: This is the recommended concept because it directly confronts the hook's premise: agents holding balances vs. agents operating credit. Contrasting a static primitive against dynamic deterministic math immediately proves why credit infrastructure is functionally distinct from basic wallet rails.

all.title: The Deterministic Solvency Gate
all.idea: An architectural state-machine diagram mapping an autonomous transaction cycle. Rather than generic flowcharts or glowing boxes, it takes the form of an engineering blueprint on dark slate: an Agent Execution Intent passes into a hardened math verification gate executing the exact Soroban smart contract formula: HF = (Sigma Collateral USD * 1e18) / Sigma Debt USD. Branching logic demonstrates deterministic solvency settlement vs auto-signed debt rebalancing before state commit.
all.why: It unpacks the internal mechanics of agentic credit rails, visually demystifying how on-chain deterministic math prevents liquidation before an agent commits borrowed funds.

all.title: The 18-Decimal Boundary
all.idea: A hero stat display centering on 1.000000000000000000 WAD—the critical solvency threshold between autonomous survival and liquidation. Rendered in clean, monumental monospace typography with an micro-annotated caliper scale measuring safe operational spread against systemic insolvency. Secondary micro-text breaks down the continuous deterministic inputs: collateral valuation, debt accumulation, and auto-signed rebalancing triggers.
all.why: It reduces the entire abstract problem of agentic credit risk to its purest mathematical reality: an 18-decimal fixed-point threshold that autonomous code cannot negotiate with.
